newsitem.title: USA: Both sides rest cases in Simpson civil trial.
newsitem.headline: Both sides rest cases in Simpson civil trial.

text.p: Both sides in the civil suit against O.J. Simpson rested their case on Thursday and the judge told jurors they would be able to start their deliberations next Thursday after closing arguments.

Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki and attorneys in the case were due to discuss jury instructions on Friday. Opening arguments were set to begin on Tuesday following Monday's Martin Luther King Day holiday, when the court was to be closed.

After Daniel Petrocelli, lead attorney for the plaintiffs, said he was resting his rebuttal case, Simpson's chief defense attorney, Robert Baker, said he too was resting. Jurors who have sat through three months of evidence, smiled and looked relieved.

The last witness for the plaintiffs was FBI shoe print expert William Bodziak, who testified that the shoes Simpson was seen wearing in 30 photographs taken at a Sept 26, 1993, Buffalo Bills football game were rare Bruno Magli Lorenzo shoes.

Bodziak had previously testified that it was the distinctive sole of the Italian designer shoes that left the bloody shoe prints leading from the scene where Simpson's ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, were stabbed and slashed to death on June 12, 1994. Simpson has denied ever owning a pair of Bruno Maglis.
Before Bodziak took the stand, former FBI photo expert Gerald Richards told the jury he had examined the pictures, taken by freelance phgotographer E.J. Flammer, and found them to be authentic.
